title: Runway friction map and short-window stability plan
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic playbook + tracker for medium-risk launches where we only get a short visibility window (hours → 3 days) to validate stability. Focus: reduce friction during ramp, define fast rollback/traffic-sculpt actions, and a minimal KPI set to decide go/no-go in the short window.

Context / when to use:
- Product features with progressive traffic windows (0.1% → 100% in <72h)
- Limited beta customers, high external visibility (integrations, partner launches)
- Workloads that materially change inference mix (batch→latency or new model families)

High-level success criteria (short-window):
- No P95 latency regression >30% over baseline at 10% traffic
- Error spike containment: 90% of error anomalies resolved or rolled back within 2h
- Cost delta: incremental gross cost of inference during validation < 15% of expected monthly allocation for the feature
- User-impact (customer facing): <0.5% of active sessions with degraded responses during ramp period

Minimal KPI set (why: keep decisions simple and automatable)
- Latency-P95 (ms): baseline vs window. Target: stay within +20% at canary; +30% during limited ramp.
- Error-rate (5xx + inference-timeouts): absolute threshold 0.3% at canary, actionable at 0.5%.
- Token-cost / 1M tokens (USD): monitor before/after quantization or model swap. Alert if +25% vs forecast.
- Success latency tail (P99): used as emergency trigger only (>2x baseline = immediate partial rollback).
- Observability coverage score: % of routes instrumented with trace/context (goal >= 90%).

Roadmap tracker snippet (short-form: one-line status for execs + action owners). Update cadence: twice daily during first 48h, hourly on launch day.
- feature: conversational-context-widening | owner: Priya Kapoor | target-window: 0.5%→10% (48h) | status: canary-configured | blockers: perf test N/A | next-action: enable 0.5% at 09:30 PST
- feature: low-cost-embedding-cache | owner: Samir Patel | target-window: 1%→25% (72h) | status: staging validation | blockers: cache-consistency bug (PROD-1127) | next-action: patch + staged deploy by 02/13
- feature: rerank-heuristic-change | owner: Diego Alvarez | target-window: 0.1%→5% (24h) | status: ready-for-canary | blockers: metric alert thresholds | next-action: merge alert updates PR

Launch readiness quick-check (pre-canary checklist; must be green to enable any traffic)
- [ ] Canary config validated (traffic slice definition, model pins, fallback mapping)
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards mapped (latency, errors, throughput, cost) + alert owners assigned
- [ ] Runbook shortlinks created + primary/secondary on-call assigned (name + number)
- [ ] Automated rollback job tested in staging (time-to-rollback < 5m)
- [ ] Canary sample dataset prepared (representative requests + edge prompts)
- [ ] Quota & capacity checks: Dedicated pools reserved or hosted burst limits confirmed
- [ ] Customer comms draft ready (if partner-facing)

Go / No-go criteria (canary → gradual ramp)
- Immediate NO-GO triggers (requires STOP and rollback): P99 > 2x baseline for >15m OR error-rate >1% sustained for 10m OR major customer API failures (severity P0).
- Actionable WARNING (pause, investigate, apply mitigations): P95 > 40% baseline, token-cost > +35%, observability coverage < 80%.
- If metrics within warning but non-critical, continue at next lower ramp step for additional 6–12h with tighter observation cadence.

Short-window stability playbook (summary, for SRE + product ops):
1) Canary enable → monitor 0–30m: critical short-list (P95, errors, p99 spikes, slow DB ops). If stable, move to 3x current traffic slice after 30m.
2) 30m–6h: hour-by-hour checks; shift to twice-per-hour ASNs (alerts to ops channel) and live doc updates.
3) 6h–24h: if no major regressions, continue ramp to target; maintain pager coverage.
4) If at any point immediate stop triggered: run rollback job, pin traffic to previous model variant, scale down autoscale target to baseline, open incident in Jira with prefilled template.

Fast rollback recipe (automation-first):
- step A: run airflow job 'traffic-sculpt' with param --slice=0 (turn off new feature) OR call routing API to switch to previous model flavor id.
- step B: force cache-invalidation for prefix caches affecting the feature (list in appendix)
- step C: set Dedicated pool min-replicas to baseline and drain new nodes
- step D: post-rollback validation (5m smoke with synthetic hits + key customer check)

Escalation ladder (who to ping)
- Primary: feature owner (see tracker)
- Secondary: product-ops lead — Maya Chen — (pager)
- SRE on-call: listed in runbook
- Eng manager for serving-runtime: Nora Liu
- Exec only if: customer SLA hit OR >30m unresolved P99 storm

Monitoring & alert templates (for owners to paste into Alertmanager)
- ALERT: Canery_P95_Deviation | expr: p95_latency_route{feature=~"conv_ctx.*"} > 1.3 * baseline | severity: warning | runbook: link
- ALERT: Canary_ErrorSpike | expr: increase(inference_errors_total[10m]) / increase(requests_total[10m]) > 0.01 | severity: critical | runbook: link

Contingency library (fast-apply mitigations)
- traffic-sculpt by locale (shrink to unaffected regions)
- degrade model: switch to quantized variant or smaller model family automatically if runtime cross-check passes
- feature flag fallback: revert to stateless path (no persistence of new context)
- throttle-heavy routes: apply per-route rate-limit for 1h and observe

Open questions / rough notes (notes-to-self style):
- How much of traffic-sculpt should be automated vs manual for partner launches? (tradeoff: speed vs accidental rollback)
- Need a templated canary sample generator for embeddings-heavy routes (PRODOPS backlog)
- Consider adding a short-window chaos test into staging (inject 10% slow nodes for 5m)

Appendix: useful links + quick commands
- rollback script (ops): github:infra/rollouts/scripts/quick-rollback.sh
- incident template: confluence:incident-templates/short-window-canary
- staging smoke command: curl -H 'X-Test-Token: smoke' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Last updated notes:
- 2025-02-12: added fast-rollback recipe, simplified KPI thresholds per SRE feedback (Diego).
- 2025-01-20: initial draft with basic checklist and tracker (Priya + Samir input).

Action items (short):

- Samir: patch cache-consistency (PROD-1127) and move to staging verification by 02/13
- Diego: add alert rules to Alertmanager and link runbook
- Maya: populate exec one-pager with top-3 risks and fallback heuristics by 02/14

-- end of doc (working draft)
